Benchmark scripts here run under `node --env-file-if-exists=.env`, so every
LOCAL_UTILITY_* value in an operator's .env is an input to a published
measurement. Node does not let --env-file override a variable already set on
the command line, so this only bites the variables a documented command does
not mention — precisely the ones nobody checks.

fix(trials): leave trial_claims correct on both keyed-checkout refusals
commits.body:
Both 409s in createTrialCheckout fire after the claim is won and before
attachTrialSession runs, so a bare throw left a session-less claim that
reads as in-flight and 409s an eligible account for two minutes. A refused
key with nothing to recover now releases the claim; a replayed complete
session attaches its id, because that trial really was spent.

commits.headline: fix(trials): make trial checkout creation idempotent per account
commits.body:
An aborted Checkout POST that Stripe is still processing has produced no
listable session yet, so the claim-token recovery finds nothing, releases
the claim, and lets a second trial out behind the first. Key the create on
the account so the retry is the same operation. A refused key is itself the
signal that a trial checkout exists: recover it or 409, never create a
second. A replayed session that is complete is a spent trial; one that is
expired gets a fresh session under the claim's own key.

commits.headline: fix(billing): say plainly when a subscription has been cancelled
commits.body:
Cancelling from the Stripe portal is cancel-at-period-end by default, so Stripe
leaves the status alone: a trialing subscriber who cancels stays `trialing`
until the period closes. Every field this dashboard stored was therefore
identical before and after, and the screen someone returned to from Stripe was
the screen they left. There was no way to tell whether it had worked.

fix(trial-g): a forearm on the ray no longer hides the wall behind it
commits.body:
TryRaycastRoom tracked the nearest non-hole hit unconditionally, and the
solver then demoted anything under MinimumRoomHitMetres to a mid-air
plant. So an arm crossing the ray at 10 cm won the nearest test and the
wall three metres behind it was never considered: the plant silently
went mid-air every time. Reject sub-minimum hits inside the loop instead,
so the surface behind them is still found.

fix(instrument): render the colour that was always being set
commits.body:
Every coloured element in the instrument is a LineRenderer or a
ParticleSystem, and both carry colour only as mesh vertex colour.
All of them shared a material built from URP/Unlit, which declares
no COLOR input, so the shader discarded every authored colour and
resolved white at full alpha. The cyan/violet/magenta palette was
computed each frame and thrown away, and because alpha was pinned
to 1 every fade in the system was inert as well.

oMLX/dflash-mlx reuses a cached snapshot only when that snapshot's ENTIRE
token sequence is a prefix of the incoming request
(dflash_mlx/cache/prefix_l1.py: `if req_tuple[:snap_len] != snap.token_ids`),
and snapshots are stored at full length — prompt AND generation. A hit
therefore requires turn N+1 to continue turn N verbatim.

without server names. That fails the new desktop-commander test in CI, and
makes any gauntlet run from a fresh worktree quietly understate production —
the exact failure mode the server-name priming was added to remove.

commits.headline: fix(voice): give request_tool_group its real schema in gauntlet toolset
commits.body:
toolDef() had no canonical entry for request_tool_group, so it fell through
to the generic unknown-tool fallback ({ arg: string }). usedEscapeHatch()
(predicates.js) scores a call against { request: ... } instead — a model
faithfully following the ONLY schema it was ever shown could never satisfy
the predicate, so the escape shape false-failed regardless of capability.
This is the root cause behind the 0/1 escape baseline tracked in #1392.

plane). Selecting an older run from the OTHER plane left the sparklines
silently describing a different plane than the results table below them.
Trends are now refetched inside the selected-run effect, scoped to
whichever run is actually selected, so both panels always agree.

fix(chat): never delete a session that owns tasks
commits.body:
`Session.tasks` uses a Cascade deletion rule, and `mergeTask` attaches
tasks to their remote session. So the seed-only cleanup could delete a
message-less session that owned tasks and take those tasks with it —
including, in the worst case, the very task being handed off. Owning
tasks now makes a session worth archiving even with no messages.

permission.

commits.body:
One `credentialsFromHub` flag covered both the endpoint and the API key,
so overriding only the key marked the endpoint user-owned too. A later

and minted a second UUID. Restrict 2xx parse retries to GET; keep 5xx
parse retries for every method.

commits.headline: fix(cloud): stop the Billing button claiming a portal request that isn't running
commits.body:
The Manage billing button shares the shell's single busy lock with the
status strip's Get early access CTA, so clicking that CTA flipped this
button's label to "Opening…" too — a specific, false claim about what
was in flight. The mirror-image case (this button's click mislabeling
the strip's CTA) was already fixed by generalizing that button's label
to "Working…" rather than adding a second per-action lock. Extend the
same already-chosen mitigation here instead of reopening that call.

commits.body:
Codex review: terminal auto-repeat emits identical KeyPressMsgs, so the
first repeat read as the confirming second press, and subsequent repeats
alternated between clearing and re-arming. Measured by mutation: twenty
repeats from one physical press dispatched sleep ten times. The
double-press guard was defeated by the simplest possible input.

commits.headline: fix(memory): give the provisioner a lifecycle instead of more patches
commits.body:
Two Codex findings on #340, but the same root cause as the previous two
rounds: `MemoryCredentialProvisioner` had no concurrency model. Round 1 it
vended over user input, round 2 it cleared its own provenance, round 3 a
late response can undo a reset. Each fix was local; the missing piece was
a lifecycle. So this adopts one rather than patching again.

commits.headline: feat(sync): enroll HTTPS signed catalogs
commits.body:
Add a transport for AutoVault Cloud catalogs over HTTPS without changing
the signed-release domain. Devices POST a public key, land pending, and
install only after signature, bundle hash, and per-file SHA-256 checks.
Bundle URLs are pinned to bundles/<bundle_hash>.json relative to
catalog.json. Beta: rotating the publishing key forces re-enrollment.

commits.body:

event at all, and pr-title.yml's `base.ref == 'main'` guard skipped its
job for the same PRs.

commits.headline: fix(trial-g): the backdrop was blurred and lit by a compression it never had
commits.body:
w describes how compressed the BAND is. A backdrop pixel's lookup relaxes
toward the plain mapping regardless of w -- that is the whole point of the
squash -- but the mip level and the brightness boost right after the sample
were still derived from w on its own. So a genuinely undistorted backdrop
sample got blurred and brightened as if it were as compressed as the band
beside it, and worse the deeper the descent ran, since w only ever shrinks.

padding. TrialAMeshBuilder.BuildParticles displaces its vertices in-shader for
orbit motion and overrides mesh.bounds afterward to compensate -- the explicit
2.5-unit cubic bound is correct for that mesh's actual on-screen extent, not
excess to trim. Reading its corners reported ~2.165 units against a 1.08-unit
rim; reading its true verti

commits.headline: fix(agents): stop parking a babysit child in unreachable awaiting_input
commits.body:
present_result() mapped a `blocked` outcome to `awaiting_input` for every task,
including the babysit follow-on child. For that child the state is unreachable
by construction: it is registered with an empty channel so no question is ever
delivered, it is absent from agentTaskQueue.tasks, and it carries no
executionSpec for resumeTask() to respawn from. Nothing can answer it.

commits.headline: test(agents): make the babysit task-store double tell the truth
commits.body:
The fake AgentTaskStore applied every status write unconditionally. The real
store's _resolveStatusUpdate() ignores a `completed` transition while the row
sits in awaiting_input with unresolved attention -- and the ignored write still
returns `true`, so the caller cannot tell it was dropped. The double also never
persisted attention_* extras at all, so the rule could not have fired even if
it were modelled.

commits.body:
The executor's local-review failure return rebuilds the result from scratch,
so a gate disposition not explicitly copied is lost. `cancelled` was dropped
there, leaving the flag dead: normalizeCapabilityBlockedResult() in worker.js
reads it to keep a user cancellation from being reclassified as a capability
block. Copied alongside `nonRetryable`, which is carried for the same reason.

commits.headline: fix(agents): abort the pre-PR preflight when the task is cancelled
commits.body:
The pre-PR ci:preflight stage this PR adds can hold the gate for up to its
full 30-minute budget. Nothing propagated cancellation into it, so a user
cancelling the coding task (or the parent deadline expiring) mid-preflight
left the gate waiting, and a successful preflight then walked straight into
_ensurePullRequest() -- opening a real PR on GitHub after the user said stop.

commits.body:
A BLE strap that drops and reconnects walks the SAME source instance through
Faulted and Scanning and back, so the reference check in Subscribe never fires.
Nothing else here noticed either: this component watches measurements, and the
defining behaviour of a disconnect is that measurements stop arriving.

commits.headline: fix(breath): a kill switch that killed half, and history that outlived its outage
commits.body:
BREATHMIRROR GATED THE BLOOM AND NOT THE SIZE. The dial is documented as a
presentation kill switch; it reached the shader channel and never reached the
transform-scale handover, so with the switch off the hole went on visibly
breathing — most obviously at high confidence or deep immersion, which is
exactly when a wearer would reach for it.

commits.headline: fix(breath): the top of the breath belonged where it happened, not where it landed
commits.body:
A strap notifies about once a second and batches every beat since the last
notification, so a resting heart routinely delivers one to two intervals per
frame and a recovery backlog delivers more. An onset found in an early element
of that batch therefore happened SECONDS before the frame reached us — and
phase was anchored at the moment of delivery, which put the top of the breath
wherever the packet happened to land.

one commit: a published claim about a wearer, surviving the thing that was

commits.headline: fix(breath): a deadband sized to the wearer, and a bed that sounds like breathing
commits.body:
THE DEADBAND WAS THE BUG, and a human found it in ninety seconds of wearing
the headset. OnsetHysteresis is a fixed 1% of the beat interval, which was
ample against the synthetic series everything here was tuned on. A real
wearer at resonance produced peak-to-peak swings of 11% to 38% — an order of
magnitude larger — and against those a 1% band is not a Schmitt trigger, it
is a bare zero-crossing test. Ripple inside a single breath tripped it.

to Dashboard's root instead of pushing.

commits.body:

frame delta. RR intervals sum to elapsed time, so the two together ran the
counter at almost exactly double speed. Consequences, all of them silent:

commits.body:
RRN goes first because nothing else in the milestone can move if the strap
is not transmitting RR intervals, and the older RR row cannot tell you that —
it falls back to 60/BPM and prints a plausible number either way. A session
spent debugging a detector that was never receiving data is the specific
failure this ordering exists to prevent.

commits.body: Three seams, all of which already existed and were waiting.

commits.headline: feat(breath): a bed that breathes slightly slower than you do
commits.body:
The other half of the biofeedback pair. The black hole MIRRORS the wearer;
this LEADS them. With no lock it simply breathes on its own — which is not a
degraded mode but the original installation: the piece breathes, the visitor
follows, nothing is measured at all.

commits.headline: feat(breath): find the breath in the space between heartbeats
commits.body:
The wearer cannot lower their heart rate on demand while working. They can
slow their breath, and slowing the breath is what drags the heart down after
it — so breathing becomes the metric and heart rate becomes the receipt.

commits.body:

code === null when a process is terminated by a signal, and `code ?? 0` mapped
that to success — so a killed ffmpeg converter would report a clean run, the
player would exit 0 after consuming its padding, and the resulting silence
would be blamed on the device. That is the exact overclaim this PR removes.

commits.headline: fix(installer): match export-prefixed assignments in every .env writer
commits.body:
Switching the readers to dotenv widened what counts as a stale credential without
widening what the removers can delete. dotenv accepts `export AUTOMEM_API_KEY=...`;
the removers matched a bare `KEY=` only. So the reader correctly identified the key
as belonging to another endpoint, asked for its removal, and the line survived —
leaving the old credential live against the new host. That leak did not exist
before the dotenv migration; it was introduced by half-applying it.

provider, .env, and provider files, and after copilot had removed stale hooks
and written new ones — so a failed mode or profile switch left the host half
reconfigured while INSTALLATION.md claimed nothing was written.

commits.body:

supplying one. A hand-edited file with text immediately after the end marker
would have run the marker into that line; the seam now puts a newline back.

commits.headline: fix(hermes): parse the provider .env with dotenv too
commits.body:
The previous commit switched install.ts and setup.ts to dotenv and claimed the
sweep was complete. A third hand-rolled reader was sitting in hermes-config.ts,
in a file this PR had already edited twice — so a provider .env written as
AUTOMEM_API_URL='https://x' or with a trailing comment compared as a different
endpoint, and a same-endpoint re-run deleted a working credential.

commits.headline: fix: refuse stray rules-file markers across all installer hosts
commits.body:
The "insert or replace a marked rules block" logic was copy-pasted into five
hosts. PR #197 hardened only the Grok copy: a file holding two start markers and
one end contains both markers, so an indexOf-based check calls it well-formed and
replaces from the first start through the end — silently deleting the second
marker and whatever the user wrote between them.

commits.headline: fix(installer): parse .env with dotenv instead of hand-rolled readers
commits.body:
Both readers that the credential pairing depends on disagreed with the parser
that actually loads these files at server startup. install.ts unwrapped only
double quotes and never stripped comments; setup.ts did the same. So a project
.env written as AUTOMEM_API_URL='https://x' or with a trailing # comment compared
as a different endpoint, and a re-run at the *same* endpoint removed a
still-valid key and left the project unauthenticated.

commits.headline: fix(openclaw): shadow rejected skill credentials instead of deleting them
commits.body:
The previous commit established that rejection has to be written as a blank
rather than omitted, because a host layers the entry env over its own. It applied
that to the Grok and Hermes entries and left OpenClaw's skill entry deleting both
names — two of three hosts, which is the same incompleteness this PR exists to
fix, one commit after stating the rule.

commits.headline: fix(uitests): seed a real plan task for UITEST_SEED_PLAN_APPROVAL
commits.body:
Codex P1, and correct. The hook reused the agent-visibility approval fixture,
whose attentionType is "permission". StructuredResponseCard.kind(forAttentionType:)
routes that through AttentionKind to .permission — a card whose controls are
permissioncard.*, not plancard.* — so testPlanCardIdentifiersResolve could never
have passed against this seed. The hook's own doc comment promised the opposite.

commits.headline: fix(installer): shadow rejected credentials at the process boundary
commits.body:
Omitting a rejected key from a server entry does not stop it reaching the server.
The host launches the child with the entry's env layered over its own
(`{...process.env, ...entry.env}`), so a shell-exported AUTOMEM_API_KEY — issued
for whatever endpoint that shell names — is inherited by a child whose URL the
entry just pointed somewhere else. Rejection has to be written, not merely
omitted.

naming endpoint A and a provider .env still holding endpoint B's token produced

credential genuinely issued for A, so it accepted the pair and wrote B's token
into A's registration — the exact disclosure the pairing was added to prevent.

`memory` registration beside the new `automem

commits.body:
Round-4 Codex P1 on #1274. Throwing on an unpersistable completion reached
the execution retry loop, where `task_completion_persist_failed` matches no
retryable pattern — so `_handleTaskFailure()` marked a task that genuinely
succeeded as failed, notified the user, and discarded the result. Surfacing
the failure was right; routing it through execution failure was not.

commits.headline: fix(agents): tell a persistence failure apart from a lost CAS
commits.body:
Round-2 Codex P1 on #1274. `completeTask()` returns false for a lost CAS and
also for a transient Prisma error, a missing row, or a refused completion.
Treating every false as "recovery won" meant a DB hiccup silently discarded a
finished task: the executor released its lane, finalization and the completion
event were suppressed, and the durable row stayed `running` with nobody told.

commits.headline: fix(agents): make the completion write a compare-and-set too
commits.body:
Codex P1 on #1274. The recovery CAS only rejected completion writes that
landed BEFORE it. A normal in-process completion finishing just after the
claim called an unconditional `agentRun.update()`, leaving durable state
`completed` while the reaper had already emitted task_review and set the
cached task to `awaiting_review`.

session id forever, so telegram--5178868641 spans 21 days / 174 messages. But
replayed history carried no timing at all, so a message sent eight days after
the previous one looked exactly like the next sentence of a continuous
exchange, and the model answered as if nothing had happened in between.

commits.body:
Sessions here are long-lived by design — a Telegram chat or Slack DM keeps one
session id forever, so telegram--5178868641 spans 21 days / 174 messages. But
replayed history carried no timing at all, so a message sent eight days after
the previous one looked exactly like the next sentence of a continuous
exchange, and the model answered as if nothing had happened in between.

commits.headline: fix(memory): stamp recalled memories with the date they were written
commits.body:
A recalled memory is a record of something that was true when it was written,
but every live renderer emitted content only. With no age signal, absolute dates
inside a memory read as current: on 2026-08-11 a voice turn recalled a trip
itinerary stored before departure and narrated it as "drive up to Hamilton today
(Aug 1)" — after the trip had already ended. The current date WAS in that system
prompt; what was missing was how old the memory was.

commits.headline: fix(mcp-sse): emit the stored date in compact recall output
commits.body:
The default (non-detailed) recall block rendered content, tags, score and ID
but dropped the memory's stored timestamp. A caller replaying that text had no
way to tell a note written today from one written six weeks ago, so absolute
dates inside the content read as if they were current — an agent recalling a
trip itinerary written before departure narrated it in the present tense ten
days after the trip ended.

commits.headline: fix(cli): re-rank corrected candidates, enforce the candidate cap per node
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. The aria-hidden correction pass now ranks the
corrected set from scratch instead of taking the first positive corrected score,
so a candidate that becomes an exact match after correction is not beaten by an
earlier prefix match. The 4000-node candidate cap is checked per node and before
each shadow-root descent rather than only on entry, and dedupe uses a Set, so a
single large root can no longer push an unbounded set through the per-node
layout and hit-test work.

commits.headline: fix(cli): walk the full ranked set, and never re-send a delivered release
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. pickClickCandidate returns `ranked` (the full ordered
set) so the aria-hidden correction pass is not capped at the three-item
runnersUp slice, which made a genuine candidate unreachable behind decoys
matching only on hidden text. The pointer sequence records which events it
delivered, so interruption cleanup cannot send a second mouseup and run
document-level release handlers twice.

commits.headline: fix(cli): confine the label-read mutation, cancel interrupted pointers, recheck disabled
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. Scoring uses plain innerText and writes nothing; only
the ranked winner is re-read with aria-hidden descendants hidden, falling through
to the next candidate if that correction kills the match. An interrupted pointer
sequence now dispatches pointercancel and mouseup on a still-connected target so
document-level pressed/drag state is not left stuck. Disabledness is rechecked
before the click event, since a mousedown handler can disable the control
mid-sequence.

commits.headline: fix(cli): exclude aria-hidden by hiding and re-reading; stop a click mid-sequence
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. aria-hidden content is excluded by setting
display:none on the outermost aria-hidden descendants, reading innerText, and
restoring the previous inline value — string subtraction could not tell which
occurrence of repeated text came from the hidden node, and was wrong in both DOM
orderings. The pointer sequence now checks isConnected between events and stops
if a handler removed the control, reporting which event it stopped before rather
than dispatching the rest at a d

commits.headline: fix(cli): score before visibility, keep disabled exact matches, use :disabled
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. The comparator now orders exact > prefix > substring
before visibility, so a visible partial match cannot outrank a hidden exact one
and dispatch a broader action. Disabled candidates are scored with the rest of
the pool and checked on the winner, so a disabled exact match is reported as
disabled rather than replaced by an enabled prefix match. Disabledness uses
matches(':disabled') plus aria-disabled instead of a fieldset[disabled] ancestor
scan, which was refusing li

hit-tests at the candidate box centre so an overlay-covered control cannot win
visible-first ranking over its live duplicate. The aria-hidden subtraction
removes one occurrence per outerm

commits.headline: ci: authenticate release-please with a PAT so release PRs run CI
commits.body:
Release PR #39 sat unmergeable for seven months. The org ruleset requires
the `test` status check, but release-please-action authored its PR with
the default GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for
GITHUB_TOKEN-authored events. ci.yml therefore never ran on the release
branch — check-runs on its head SHA returned total_count 0 — so the
required check could never appear and the PR could never merge.

object form of extra-files. `{"type": "generic", ...}` would have failed
validation and broken the release-please run outright — generic files
must be given as a plain path string.

commits.headline: fix(mcp): close the second Codex wave — stale tools, truncated urls, deep payloads
commits.body:
Plain coalescing of tools/list_changed left the hub serving stale schemas
indefinitely. A tools/list response describing state A and a later
notification announcing state B can arrive in the same stdout chunk;
handleServerOutput parses that chunk synchronously, so B joined A's
already-answered fetch and B was never requested. Confirmed with a
two-notifications-in-one-chunk probe: one tools/list call, tools stuck at A.
A dirty flag now forces exactly one trailing fetch, so a burst costs two
round

commits.headline: fix(mcp): close the three P1 gaps Codex found on the lifecycle PR
commits.body:
closeRemoteServer never reached client.close()/transport.close() when
terminateSession() threw synchronously: Promise.allSettled evaluates its
argument array before it is called, so the throw escaped the whole helper.
Shutdown then cleared the maps with a live HTTP client and session behind
them — a leak on every such shutdown. Both allSettled sites now capture a
synchronous throw as a rejection.

commits.headline: fix(frontier): never certify queue health from the dry-run subset
commits.body:
Codex P1 round 2: `--dry-run` leaves the cycle's candidateDbPath null, so the
health report fell back to `topCandidates` — priority-sorted and `--limit`
capped — and an aged persisted candidate absent from that subset produced
`status: "healthy"`. Same false-healthy shape as the 200-row window, one
branch over.

commits.headline: fix(frontier): scan every tracked candidate for the SLA check
commits.body:
Codex P1: `listCandidates` clamps to 200 rows per status, sorts by priority,
and offers no offset — so past 200 tracked rows the SLA scan silently dropped
exactly the aged low-priority candidate it exists to find, and the report
claimed "healthy" on a queue it had not fully read. That is the same
aggregate-hides-the-individual failure #1025 is about, one level up.

commits.headline: fix(sync): route HubSyncService print() error paths through AppLog
commits.body:

watchdog reparent and SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP. Capture parentPid before
any await; unit tests assert stdin EOF alone does not exit.

commits.headline: fix: soft-close stdin EOF so one-shot pipe calls can finish
commits.body:
Hard process.exit on stdin end/close raced the documented
`echo … | npm start` tool probe (AGENTS.md) and could kill in-flight
handlers before the MCP response was written. Close the transport on EOF
and let the event loop drain; parent-watchdog + signals still hard-exit
orphans that keep stdin open.

commits.headline: fix(voice): await prior interrupt teardown in dispose() via pendingPlayerTeardown
commits.body:
killPlayer() nulls the shared player reference synchronously while the
underlying process exits asynchronously. When shutdown follows shortly after
a barge-in interrupt(), dispose() saw player === null and resolved early
instead of awaiting the in-flight teardown, racing the unref'd SIGKILL
backstop.

final merge so intermediate library LOCATION (pre-strip) cannot fail
the build; (2) EnsurePermission collapses uses-permission-sdk-23
alongside uses-permission so unflagged sdk-23 SCAN cannot undermine

commits.headline: fix(ble): session-scoped queue counters for reservation undo
commits.body:
Codex P2: floor-at-zero undo still crossed sessions — a prior-session
rollback could decrement the live bag after End/Begin. Callbacks now
close over a per-Begin SessionQueue bag so dead-session undos only
mutate abandoned counters.

commits.headline: fix(android): ignore tools:node=remove location strip markers
commits.body:
Codex P2 on #24: pre-merge RequireNoLocationPermission treated
uses-permission(-sdk-23) tools:node=remove as real declarations and
aborted before the merger could strip transitive LOCATION. Skip remove
markers; post-merge Gradle gate stays authoritative.

commits.headline: fix(ble): floor reservation undo so End cannot drive counters negative
commits.body:
Codex P2 on #26: after IsLiveSession fails, a bare Decrement can race
DiscardPending's zeroing and leave _queued*Count at -1, under-counting
the next session. UndoReservation CAS-floors at zero so End's reset
absorbs the reservation cleanly.

commits.headline: fix(android): cover sdk-23 permissions and canonical survivors
commits.body:
Honor uses-permission-sdk-23 in C# and Gradle location gates so AAR
declarations cannot bypass the post-merge check. When collapsing Bluetooth
permission duplicates, keep an unrestricted survivor (not a maxSdkVersion or
tools:node=remove peer) and strip leftover constraints. Neutralize orphan
BEGIN markers during gate recovery so a later re-export cannot delete
legitimate Gradle that followed a partial injection.

commits.headline: fix(ble): session-safe queue counters, monotonic resync, GATT identity gate
commits.body:
Codex second pass on PR #26:
- Do not decrement live queue counters when dropping stale-session items;
  re-validate the closed-over generation after reserving a slot and undo if
  End/Begin already DiscardPending'd.
- RequestStateResync uses a monotonic CAS so an older generation cannot
  overwrite a newer overflow stamp.
- onCharacteristicChanged rejects closed || g != gatt like every other GATT
  callback, so a late notification from a closed client cannot deliver into
  a rebound session.

stamp a stale Failed/frame as current. Install fresh delegates that close
over the generation at Begin, unhook those exact instances on End, and
stamp overflow resync the same way. Deterministic EditMode coverage via

commits.headline: fix(heart-rate): round-trip empty BLE capture frames
commits.body:
Empty BLE notifications are intentional RawFrameReceived events, but
Serialize wrote them as "<millis> " and TryParse rejected empty hex —
and full Trim dropped the trailing space so the line looked like a
missing column. Accept empty hex payloads and TrimStart-only so one
zero-length notification no longer makes a whole session unreplayable.

commits.headline: fix(build): reject NO_BLE heart-rate on non-dev release builds

and network bootstrap stay out of the release player — a silent heartbeat-less
APK (issue #12). Fail closed at build time with a clear error before settings
mutation or BuildPipeline, and cover the policy + builder path with editor tests.

commits.headline: feat(trial-g): settle the throw feel, and give the HUD an off switch
commits.body:
throwCruiseSpeed 0.08, settled on device, and it took three passes because I had
the wrong model of the dial. Cruise is a speed FLOOR, not just a decay target:
nothing travels slower than it, so a gentle toss is accelerated UP to it. At 0.5
every throw felt forceful -- "if I just give it a gentle toss it goes a bit faster
than I would expect" -- and at the original 0.075 a throw died in five feet. 0.08
keeps a gentle toss gentle; the six-second half-life is what carries a hard one.
Half-life own

commits.body:

no longer applies any influence, but EndLassoDrive's hover branch still clamped
the body to HoverMaximumSpeed (0.18 m/s) and replaced the flight envelope. So a
passive off-hand hover simply drifting out of view still destroyed a live throw --
and it bypassed the downgrade guard completely, because the clamp happens there
rather than through CalibrateAndArmRelease.

_FieldExpansion and _InflowRate are amplitude dials that BlackHoleHeartbeatChannels
republishes as tuning constants every frame, so folding them straight into
radialScale produced a fixed offset rather than a breath -- the Field | Inflow role

commits.headline: fix(starfield): size mesh bounds to the dials' actual permitted expansion
commits.body:
TrialGStarfieldMesh.Create padded bounds by a flat 25% over the baked
volume, but TrialGStarfield.shader's Vert can scale a star's radial
distance by up to 2x (radialScale = 1 + _FieldExpansion - _InflowRate,
each clamped to [0, 1] by BlackHoleVisualTuning). fieldExpansion ships at
1.0 today, so a low inflowRate during a tuning sweep could pop stars out
of the frustum edge -- Unity culls against these baked bounds, not the
vertex shader's runtime result.

commits.headline: fix(starfield): pick the volume's actual longest axis for the sampling fallback
commits.body:
TrialGStarfieldMesh.SampleHome's exhausted-rejection-sampling fallback
always placed its point on Z at the volume's longest half-extent, even
when X or Y was the longer axis. An 8x4x2 volume's longest axis is X, so
the fallback returned (0, 0, 4) -- 4m out on a Z axis whose half-extent is
only 1m, outside both the volume and the mesh bounds.

_MinPullDistance only ever floored the pull-strength denominator in
TrialGStarfield.shader's Vert; the destination lerp toward the singularity
was unbounded, so a close pass could still carry a star to within ~4% of
the singularity despite the dial. The comfort guarantee it advertises --
no star ever yanked through the wearer's face -- was false as written.

Shader_ExposesTheBoundedRingRadius asserted _ShockwaveAmount defaults to 0
but left _ShockwavePhase's -1 default unpinned. -1 is the load-bearing
value -- it is what keeps Vert's `if (_ShockwavePhase >= 0.0)` branch

the branch would go live every frame on an unwritten material; the amount
defaulting to 0 only zeroes the magnitude, not the branch.

shader (fill-rate budget, not fragment) and dissolves before it reaches
the wearer, and is gated on _SingularityWS.w the same way the pull is, so
a disabled channel writer cannot fire a ring from a ghost position.

commits.headline: fix(starfield): stop a disabled channel writer from publishing a ghost singularity
commits.body:

true (by design, to avoid re-latching against the pre-disable position), which
meant it published w=1 with the stale last-known position. BlackHoleVisualTuning's
DefaultPullStrength (1f) and DefaultInfallRate (0.35f) are already non-zero, so
the moment a future task wires those dials to the shader, a disabled writer would
leave every star pulling toward a black hole that is no longer there.

falloff from _SingularityWS, a hash-phased per-star home -> horizon -> home
infall cycle, and an alpha fade so a star reads as consumed rather than
teleported. _PullStrength and _InfallRate default to 0, so a material
nobody writes to keeps rendering exactly as it did before this task.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): gate calm growth on trustworthy signal
commits.body:
BlackHoleHeartbeatPulse.calmTarget was scaled by PulseAmplitude alone,
which ramps toward 1 on measurement freshness regardless of contact
state. A contact-capable strap that keeps streaming NotDetected after
it comes off therefore kept being treated as genuine calmness, holding

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): verify arrival distance before raising SummonArrived
commits.body:
TrialGPhysicsController ends a recall (EndRecallDrive) purely because
its fixed-duration curve elapsed, whether or not the body actually
reached the target -- a room collider blocking the dynamic body ends
the drive the exact same way as a clean delivery. TrialGSummonController
read IsRecalling == false alone as "arrived" and raised SummonArrived
unconditionally, so a recall blocked behind a wall could still announce
arrival while the black hole stayed far outside ArrivalDistance.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): give the summon flash a signal-independent gain
commits.body:
The summon gesture works with no heart-rate source connected, but its
body flash was multiplied by `warm` (_WarmColor * _WarmAmount), and
_WarmAmount is 0 by default until a live rate produces calmness. In a
release session where BLE has not connected -- the default state for
any wearer without a strap -- the hand rings would announce a summon
arrival while the black hole itself answered with nothing.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): reject non-finite values in the UDP tuning protocol
commits.body:
float.TryParse accepts "NaN" and "Infinity" as well-formed numbers, and
neither Mathf.Clamp nor Mathf.Clamp01 sanitizes them -- both of Clamp's
comparisons are false for NaN, so it passes straight through. A message
like "beatsizeamount=NaN" over UDP could therefore reach
BlackHoleVisualTuning.BeatSizeAmount, which now feeds directly into
pulseTarget.localScale (BlackHoleHeartbeatPulse.LateUpdate), poisoning
the black hole's transform.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): gate published beat energy on trustworthy signal
commits.body:
BlackHoleHeartbeatChannels published _BeatEnergy unconditionally even
when BlackHoleBeatTreatmentMath.HasTrustworthySignal was false (e.g. a
contact-capable strap reporting NotDetected). PulseAmplitude ramps up
from measurement freshness alone, so the envelope stayed nonzero and
TrialAEmissive/TrialAParticles kept brightening and expanding the body
after the strap was removed, contradicting the "strap removed -> warm
response goes to nothing" acceptance criterion.

fix(heartbeat): blend treatment weights instead of cutting between them
commits.body:
The spec asks for continuous weights so crossing a treatment boundary
does not pop. TreatmentBlendHalfLife existed as a pinned constant with
nothing reading it — BlackHoleHeartbeatChannels assigned
ResolveWeights' output to _weights directly, so crossing the 1.5 m
distance band was a one-frame cut from (size 1.0, ember 0.7) to
(shockwave 1.0). The half-life's own contract test asserted only the
constant's value, which would pass against this no-op.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): surface emberAmount and shockwaveAmount on the tuning HUD
commits.body:
The tuning page showed MIX/BAND/FORCED/FIELD/INFLOW/WARM/BEAT/LAST but
omitted emberAmount and shockwaveAmount — the one dial the plan
explicitly leaves unsettled pending the user's on-device re-judgement.
During that session the wearer would turn the shockwave dial and get no
on-screen confirmation it landed, only the LAST line's raw echo of the
last accepted message, which is one message stale.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): wire BeatSizeAmount into the pulse's size treatment
commits.body:
BeatSizeAmount was advertised by tune-udp.py, parsed and clamped by
BlackHoleVisualTuning.TryApply, reset by ResetToDefaults, pinned by a
test and displayed live on the tuning HUD as "BEAT: 0.06" — but nothing
consumed it. A dial that reports success and does nothing is worse than
an absent one: a developer sends beatSizeAmount=0.3, watches the HUD
confirm it, and sees no change.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): give the warm gate a floor the tuning rig can reach
commits.body:
_WarmAmount gated every warm treatment (ember, shockwave ring, breath
bloom, summon flash) as calmness * WarmAmount. Calmness is exactly 0 at
90+ BPM and ~0.39 at a normal standing 75 BPM, so at an elevated heart
rate treatment selection had no visible effect at all — and because
WarmAmount was a multiplier, sending warmAmount=1 over UDP could not
force it back on. The tuning rig structurally could not reach the
failure it exists to let a developer diagnose.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): clear the tuning HUD page before redrawing it
commits.body:
RedrawTuningPage() drew directly onto the persisted pixel buffer without
clearing it first, unlike Redraw()'s page-0 path. DrawText/DrawGlyph only
set lit pixels, never clear the surrounding cell, so BAND, FORCED, and
LAST — the fields most likely to shrink between redraws while parked on
page 1 during live tuning — could leave stale glyph fragments from the
previous, longer text bleeding through. Mirrors the same full-buffer
FillRect(BackgroundColor) that Redraw() already does before drawing.

prs.title: feat(campaigns): PATCH existing broadcasts
prs.body:
## Summary
- Draft campaigns can be updated in place via `PATCH /api/campaigns/:id` (name, subject, preview, markdown, audience).
- Missing IDs return 404. Once a campaign leaves `draft` (`sending` / `sent`), PATCH returns 409 so queue batches keep a stable payload for batch idempotency keys.
- The update is a compare-and-swap (`WHERE status = 'draft'`), so a concurrent send that flips status cannot be overwritten by a later PATCH.

Stdio MCP servers can leak forever when a client (Claude Desktop / Cursor / Grok / Codex) abandons a session but an intermediate wrapper (`npx` / `npm exec` / launcher) keeps the stdin write-end open. No EOF arrives, the process stays in the event loop, and repeated leaks cause multi-GB swap thrashing.
